item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe release 2.08, d1vmga_ (1vmg A:) and d1y6xa1 (1y6x A:7-93) are not placed in the same family: d1vmga_ is in family a.204.1.2, MazG-like, while d1y6xa1 is in family a.204.1.4, HisE-like (PRA-PH). They do share the same superfamily a.204.1, all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases, within fold a.204 and class a, so SCOPe supports a remote evolutionary relationship at the superfamily level, not a close family-level relationship. The supported conclusion is common ancestry/structural homology at the all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatase superfamily level. It would go beyond this evidence to transfer the specific HisE phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase function, MazG-like substrate specificity, catalytic details, active-site equivalence, or detailed template-based functional annotation between the two domains without independent sequence, structural active-site, genomic, or biochemical evidence. A template from the other family may be useful for broad fold/superfamily context, but not as sufficient evidence for precise function transfer or for choosing same-family representatives.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/releases","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116993","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140797","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101385","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456"]}]}
